assessment.overall_rationale: The replicates contain three strongly corresponding programs: core ciliogenesis, endothelial ciliary mechanosensing, and FZD4/GATA2/ENG-mediated CNS vascular-barrier regulation, with weaker cross-pair overlap driven mainly by ciliary dependence or shared brain-endothelial context.

pair_scores.rationale: Both modules describe the same core ciliogenesis machinery, including basal-body docking, transition-zone organization, IFT, and BBSome-mediated trafficking with nearly identical genes.
The right module uses the same ciliary apparatus but shifts the central meaning from organelle construction and trafficking to endothelial flow sensing and BBB maturation.
Core cilia construction is mechanistically distinct from FZD4, GATA2, and Endoglin control of endothelial identity and vascular-barrier formation.
Endothelial mechanosensing requires the core ciliogenesis machinery described on the right, but its defining output is shear-stress detection rather than cilium assembly itself.
Both modules interpret the ciliary genes as enabling blood-flow mechanosensing in brain endothelial cells, with the right module adding BBB maturation as a downstream outcome.
The modules share brain-endothelial and vascular-barrier context, but ciliary shear sensing differs centrally from Wnt/Norrin, GATA2, and Endoglin regulation.
FZD4/GATA2/Endoglin-mediated CNS vascular regulation and core cilium assembly have no substantial shared mechanism or asserted output.
Both concern brain endothelial maturation and BBB function, but one centers on receptor and transcriptional regulation while the other centers on ciliary mechanotransduction.
Both modules describe the same FZD4-dependent Norrin/Wnt, GATA2, and Endoglin regulatory program governing CNS angiogenesis, endothelial identity, and BBB integrity.
